## Start with one representative question

[S03-Q032](#S03-Q032)

<p>Given Department and Employee in a one-to-many relationship, write a query returning departments with more than three employees. Explain how you would check the result.</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Write and verify a department headcount query against an exact reporting contract.</p>

<ul>
<li>Choose the department identity that each output row represents.</li>
<li>Justify the counted expression, threshold and preservation of empty departments.</li>
<li>Detect incorrect results with boundary data and an added one-to-many join.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

No catalog prerequisite. Establish the terms and scenario assumptions in the foundation questions before progressing; a published lesson is not evidence that you know them.

<p>Begin with the source task: return departments with more than three employees. A query can run successfully and still count the wrong thing; follow the joined rows into groups, then check the report&#x27;s boundary cases. Zero-count reports are a changed contract, not a hidden requirement of the original task.</p>

### S03-Q032 · Application

<p>Given Department and Employee in a one-to-many relationship, write a query returning departments with more than three employees. Explain how you would check the result.</p>

**Source:** [S03-Q032](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q032)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S03-Q032](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q032)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Given `Department` and `Employee` in a one-to-many relationship, return departments having more than three employees.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Translate the relationship and threshold into one result row per department. The task asks for an exact count contract, not an approximate headcount.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Implement and verify grouping at the correct department identity.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Assume unique, non-null department and employee IDs and one department per employee. Count all employees; active-only and zero-count reports are added variations, not the original requirement.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Explains the grouping identity, counted value and exact threshold.</li>
<li>Checks zero, three and four employees, duplicate department names and nullable employee names.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Grouping only by a display name or interpreting &#x27;more than three&#x27; as including three.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would the query change if every department must be returned, including those with no employees?</li>
<li>What could change if another one-to-many table is joined before counting?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>Design a headcount endpoint for departments that may share names and employees whose names may be missing. First implement the source threshold report, then an added report including empty departments. A later change joins employee skills, with several skills per person: show how you would detect a headcount regression using explicit expected rows.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Produces a query for ordinary data and explains the more-than-three threshold.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Defends grouping and counting against duplicate names, NULLs and join multiplication; compares results for each declared report contract.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>No query, expected boundary rows or observed output is supplied; a fluent explanation alone does not establish correctness.</p>
